newsitem.title: USA: Senate could not address tobacco until autumn.
newsitem.headline: Senate could not address tobacco until autumn.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said Thursday if the states and the tobacco industry reach a deal on pending lawsuits, the Senate could not take up related legislation until at least September or October.
"We are pretty much locked out of anything of that nature probably until September or October," the Mississippi Republican told reporters.
Lott and House Speaker Newt Gingrich, a Georgia Republican, have both expressed doubts in recent weeks about whether Congress would be able to enact tobacco legislation this session.

Any deal negotiated by the 40 state attorneys general and the tobacco industry would require action from Congress. Many Congressional sources have said they expect that to be a cumbersome piece of legislation, which likely would be subject to a tug-of-war between anti-smoking advocates and lawmakers from tobacco-growing states.
The fate of any legislation also would depend in part on how the public health community regards any proposed settlement.

Former Surgeon General C. Everett Koop and former Food and Drug Commissioner David Kessler have been leading an effort to have major health organisations try to reach a consensus on whether any settlement proposal will be a genuine advance for their public health agenda.
